what: Pegasystems sells software that large companies use to automate workflows and customer service, such as processing insurance claims, handling bank customer requests and running call centres. It increasingly sells it as a cloud subscription and adds AI tools to design and run these processes.
customers: Large banks, insurers, telecom companies, healthcare firms and governments.
money: Pega Cloud and term licences, sold as recurring contracts.
moat: Its software is embedded in the core processes of large organisations, which makes switching expensive and slow.
risks: Competition from ServiceNow and Salesforce, which are much larger.
Lumpy licence revenue makes quarterly results noisy.
Fear that AI agents will replace workflow software has hit valuations across the sector.
Diluted shares rose from 163M in 2021 to 185M in 2025.
opportunities: Free cash flow grew from $29M in 2021 to $491M in 2025.
Revenue reached $1.75B in 2025, up from $1.21B in 2021.
The forward P/E of about 10 is low for a profitable software company.
Seven analysts average a target near $41, about 50% above the price.
watch: Growth in annual contract value and Pega Cloud.
view: Pegasystems has transformed its finances: free cash flow went from almost nothing in 2021 to about $490 million in 2025, and the company is now solidly profitable. Yet at about 10 times forward earnings, the market prices it as if AI will make workflow software obsolete.

That fear is the key issue. If AI agents can do what Pega’s workflows do, its moat narrows. But Pega is building AI into its platform, and large banks and insurers rarely rip out the systems running their core processes.

This turns on whether contract value keeps growing as customers adopt its AI tools. I think the market is too pessimistic and that 10 times earnings for a profitable, cash-generative software company is cheap, but it is a contrarian position.
bull: AI features drive new contracts and the market re-rates a cash-rich software company.
bear: AI agents commoditise workflow software and growth stalls.
